full_judgment: 36. The learned Advocate for the appellant in support of his submissions referring some decisions in the case of Masud and others vs State reported in 3 BLC 107 and in the case of Akkas Miah and others reported in 25 DLR, 398, submits that non-examination of all the prosecution witnesses in this case mentioned in the charge-sheet raises a presumption against the prosecution to the effect that had they been examined, they would not have supported the prosecution case. But, on perusal of those decisions, we find that the facts and circumstances of those cases are distinguishable from that of the present case and we hold that when the prosecution has already been able to prove the charge levelled against the appellant it is not necessary to examine all the charge-sheeted witnesses.
